annotations.title: Export the rows an import can't take

description: Make a CSV file of the rows of an open import that would fail at `revision` under its current mapping and settings: the file's own header row, every cell as it was written, and a last column with the first reason in `locale` (the workspace's language when left out). Fix the rows, then import that file: it reads back in as it is. It answers a link, not the file: download it with a plain GET, no key, within 10 minutes, at most 3 times. Anyone who has the link can read the file, so share it only with whoever should see these contacts. The rows are counted now (`count`), the same ones `preview.failed` counts; the file is written when you download it, and the link stops working if the import changes first. 409 serverErrors.importStale when `revision` is not the current one, 409 serverErrors.importNoFailures when no row fails, 409 serverErrors.importCommitted and serverErrors.importExpired when the file is gone: a committed import keeps no cells, so its failed rows can't come back, and you upload the file again. At most 10 files a minute per workspace.

locale.description: The language of the file's reasons and its separator: a comma in en, a semicolon in pt-BR and es. The workspace's language when left out.

revision.description: The revision whose dry run you read. If the import changed since, nothing is made and it answers 409 serverErrors.importStale, with the current revision in details.revision.
